newsitem.title: CHINA: China state cotton purchases fall sharply yr-on-yr.
newsitem.headline: China state cotton purchases fall sharply yr-on-yr.

text.p: Chinese state purchases of cotton in the autumn purchasing season have dropped sharply compared with the same period of 1995, the Xinhua news agency said on Wednesday.
Chinese authorities had bought 1.60 million tonnes of ginned cotton by November 20, down 942,500 tonnes compared with the same period in last year's season, the official agency said.
The cotton purchasing season lasts from autumn to spring.

State cotton purchasing this year was brisk in eastern Zhejiang province, while the volume bought in other cotton producing areas appeared lower than last year, Xinhua said. It gave no details or explanation for the drop in purchases.
Chinese officials have predicted that despite a small reduction in the area planted, this year's cotton harvest will be similar in scale to last year when output totalled 4.4 million tonnes.
